### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
In the processing and presentation of peptides of extracellular origin, the TAP proteins transport peptides into the endoplasmic reticulum for loading onto MHC class I molecules. The tapasina assists in the assembly of MHC class II molecules and facilitates peptide binding. The HLA-DM molecule acts as a chaperone for MHC class II molecules, aiding in peptide exchange. The proteasome degrades intracellular proteins into peptides, generating antigenic peptides for presentation. The HLA-B molecules present peptides to cytotoxic T cells, initiating an immune response. Relevant evidence includes the interaction of the multicatalytic endopeptidase complex with cells and peptides, peptides causing immunity, and the interaction between T-lymphocytes, cytotoxic cells, and interferon-alpha in immune responses.
